messages.subject: log-likelihood in JAGS
parts:
Hello there,

I am trying to fit a multi-state occupancy model in JAGS. Below is the model example for my "null" model (only p varies by occasion, but no covariates of psi or r):

cat("
    model  { 
    # Priors
    # detection (static)
    p1[t] ~ dunif(0, 1)
    p2[t] ~ dunif(0,1)
    delta ~ dunif(0,1)
    
    # occurrence (static)
    psi ~ dunif(0, 1)
    # a0 ~ dunif(-10,10)
    # a1 ~ dunif(-10,10)

    # reproductive value (variable)
    r ~ dunif(0, 1)
    # b0 ~ dunif(-10,10)
    # b1 ~ dunif(-10,10)
    
    # Define state vector
    for (i in 1:M){
    phi[i,1] <- 1 - psi[i]            # Prob. of non-occupation
    phi[i,2] <- psi[i] * (1-r[i])        # Prob. of occupancy without repro
    phi[i,3] <- psi[i] * r[i]            # Prob. of occupancy and repro

    # landscape effects on r
    # logit(r[i]) <- b0 # model for r
    # logit(psi[i]) <- a0 # model for psi
    }

    # Define observation matrix
    # Order of indices: true state, time, observed state
    for (t in 1:T){
    p[1,t,1] <- 1
    p[1,t,2] <- 0
    p[1,t,3] <- 0

    p[2,t,1] <- 1-p1[t]
    p[2,t,2] <- p1[t]
    p[2,t,3] <- 0

    p[3,t,1] <- 1 - p2[t]
    p[3,t,2] <- p2[t] * (1 - delta)
    p[3,t,3] <- p2[t] * delta
    }
    
    # State-space likelihood
    # State equation: model of true states (z)
    for (i in 1:M){
    z[i] ~ dcat(phi[i,])
    }
    
    # Observation equation
    for (i in 1:M){
    for (t in 1:T){ 
    y[i,t] ~ dcat(p[z[i],t,])

    log.lik0[i,t]<-logdensity.cat(y[i,t],p[z[i],t,])
    } #t
    } #i
    
    # Derived quantities
    for (i in 1:M){
    occ1[i] <- equals(z[i], 1)
    occ2[i] <- equals(z[i], 2)
    occ3[i] <- equals(z[i], 3)

    log.lik[i] <- sum(log.lik0[i,]) 
    }
    
    n.occ[1] <- sum(occ1[]) # Sites in state 1
    n.occ[2] <- sum(occ2[]) # Sites in state 2
    n.occ[3] <- sum(occ3[]) # Sites in state 3
    }
    
    ",file="mstate.occ.kan.txt")

My question pertains to obtaining a log-likelihood matrix which I can then use to estimate LOOIC using the LOO package (Vehtari, Gelman & Gabry, 2017a,2017b). As you can see above, I have estimated log.lik at site i at occasion t as:     

log.lik0[i,t]<-logdensity.cat(y[i,t],p[z[i],t,])
log.lik[i] <- sum(log.lik0[i,]) 

My understanding of how to implement this is pretty poor, and I am therefore unsure if this is the correct approach... Has anyone done similar, and if so, is this along the right lines or completely off-base? 

Also, apologies if this is not relevant here, but I was unsure where to post. Please let me know a more relevant google group/forum if it is not.

Cheers,

Andrew

messages.subject: log-likelihood in JAGS
parts:
Hi,
FWIW, the hmecology google group is good for questions like these.
Anyway, you want to marginalize over z. It’s not terrible for this model, something like:
Loglike[i]= log(
Pr(z=1)*prod(pr(y[i, 1:t]|z=1))+
Pr(z=2)*prod(pr(y[i, 1:t]|z=2))+
Pr(z=3)*prod(pr(y[i, 1:t]|z=3))
)

Hopefully the distinction between this and your code makes sense: you are taking log (pr(y[it] | whatever z[i] is during the iteration in question)).

Don’t know the best way to code it in JAGS. You might be ok working on the real scale, or you might have to use log and exp creatively in a few places to avoid underflow. Might be easier to run calculations in r after fitting?

John
